messages.text: Monday, November 9 · Canton, Michigan
Bingo asymptotics, quiet overcast skies, and the rhythm of the week

Sunday brings a steady, overcast stillness to Canton as the local calendar turns toward mid-month commitments. Science offers a look at the deep geological forces shaping our continents and the quantum mechanics challenging our sense of objective reality.
Expect an overcast day with a high near 55 degrees and a low around 38 degrees.
The sun rises at 7:17 AM and sets at 5:18 PM, with a new moon that is 0.2% illuminated.
A quiet Sunday for inquiry and song

The Math Grad Show and Tell seminar explores the surprising asymptotics of bingo at 3 PM in Ann Arbor's East Hall. Later, The Ark hosts an open stage at 8 PM for those wanting to share music or listen.
A meeting is scheduled for November 11 at 6:30 PM.
Investments in local support and policy

The KeyBank Foundation has invested $250,000 to expand the Shelter Association of Washtenaw County's warming center and resource hub in Ypsilanti. Meanwhile, Congresswoman Debbie Dingell is proposing a Data Center Bill of Rights to address infrastructure and environmental transparency.
Looking toward the week
Prepare for the 862 Meeting taking place this Tuesday evening.

Tuesday, November 10 · Canton, Michigan
Overcast skies and the hidden labor behind our digital world
A mild, gray Monday brings temperatures reaching the mid-sixties before a shift in the pattern. Today's focus turns toward the unseen costs of modern technology and the weight of historical memory.
Expect an overcast day with a high near 64°F and a low around 40°F.
The sun rises at 7:19 AM and sets at 5:17 PM, with a new moon that is 1.1% illuminated.
Thoughtful evenings in Ann Arbor

For a critical look at technology, attend the film screening In the Belly of AI at the Ann Arbor District Library at 6:00 PM. Alternatively, hear local musicians perform at The Ark at 7:30 PM to benefit the Veterans for Peace scholarship.
A community meeting is scheduled for tomorrow, November 11, at 6:30 PM.
Washtenaw County resource expansion

The KeyBank Foundation has provided a $250,000 investment to expand the Shelter Association of Washtenaw County's warming center and daytime resource hub in Ypsilanti. This funding aims to support facility costs and food services to better serve 40 people daily.
Looking toward the week
Mark your calendar for the United Way Make a Difference Day coming up on November 14 at 9:00 AM.
